newsitem.title: SWAZILAND: Golf-Henning takes two-shot lead in Royal Swazi Open.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Henning takes two-shot lead in Royal Swazi Open.

text.p: South Africa's Nic Henning, sparked by some pinpoint iron play, opened up a two-shot lead after successive rounds of 66 at the halfway stage of the 1997 Royal Swazi Open on Friday.

While first-round leader Desvonde Botes followed up his opening course record of 63 with a one-over-par 73, Henning hardly faltered over the picturesque Royal Swazi Golf Club layout as he moved to 132 - and 12-under for the tournament.

England-born Chris Davison fired a second successive 67 to move into second place on 134 at 10-under-par, to be joined later by South African Warrick Druian who vaulted up the leaderboard with an eight-under-par 64.

Two more South Africans, Tjaart van der Walt (66) and Callie Swart (69), shared fourth place on 135 while 1996 Zambian Open champion Botes was a further shot back on 136 with compatriot Mark Murless (66).

Despite tougher pin positions for the second round, the 27-year-old Henning, son of well-known South African professional Graham, stormed out in only 31 with a string of five birdies on his front nine.
He then came back in 35, after dropping only his second shot of the tournament when he pulled his tee shot left on the par-four 16th.

Henning, who also changed to a Great Big Bertha driver for February's South African Open, feels his golf has been consistent for most of the 1996-97 Southern African tour: "I've been playing well the whole season without having much luck. Maybe that'snow beginning to change!"
The halfway cut was made at one-over-par 145 with 68 players advancing through to Saturday's third round.
